independent_reviews.review_scope: Read-only independent mathematical and source-contract review of the actual K-transform calculus, Frobenius realization, cone spectral argument, all four stability equivalences, and the actual K-transform Neumann inverse and canonical witness.

evidence.claim: The derivative is the genuine Frechet derivative of the stated integral K-transform.
evidence.assessment: Passed F20. The ordinary total matrix inverse is differentiated on an actual open invertibility neighborhood. Compact support constructs uniform local domination and integrability; no conditions outside the support are assumed. The two resolvent expressions have the correct noncommutative order.

evidence.claim: The whitened coefficient and derivative congruence are the source objects.
evidence.assessment: Passed F21. Z is sqrt(S) T sqrt(S), C is Z (I+Z)^(-1), and C is Hermitian even for indefinite T. Both the derivative congruence and quadratic identity retain the exact inverse-square-root factors and alpha^(-1).

evidence.claim: The operator norm is the real Frobenius Hilbert operator norm.
evidence.assessment: Passed. The type synonym has a separately constructed real inner-product core equal to frobInner; its norm is definitionally frobNorm. The restricted operator has exactly the actual source integral action. Its norm is not the ambient matrix spectral-operator norm.

evidence.claim: Cone positivity is distinct from Hilbert positivity, and indefinite coefficients are permitted.
evidence.assessment: Passed F22. The argument uses PSD preservation of each Hermitian sandwich and Frobenius symmetry. Positive/negative spectral parts give same-norm absolute-Rayleigh majorants; sphere maximization yields a nonzero PSD eigenmatrix at the full operator norm. No nonnegative Hilbert quadratic-form hypothesis is introduced, so negative eigenvalues are allowed.

evidence.claim: All four advertised stability conditions are equivalent on their actual source domains.
evidence.assessment: Passed. The first condition quantifies every nonzero actual Hermitian matrix. The norm uses the exact Frobenius restriction. Y and B are actual positive-definite matrices, with Y-L(Y) and DK(S)[B] positive definite. Proved inverse congruences transport the witnesses, Hermitian domain and nonzeroness in both directions. The final theorem retains nonempty dimension, alpha>0, compactly supported probability law, S>0, and support-only strict gaps.

evidence.claim: The Neumann inverse is the actual inverse and preserves the PSD cone.
evidence.assessment: Passed F23 at both generic and actual-K layers. The operator is the genuine sum of powers, proved equal to Ring.inverse(I-L). PSD preservation follows from PSD finite sums and the closed PSD cone. The actual-K wrapper uses the exact source Frobenius restriction and constructs Y=Ring.inverse(I-L) I, with Y positive definite, Y>=I, and the exact matrix identity Y-L(Y)=I.

baseline_audit.title: Operator-monotone functions have a spectral-norm modulus of continuity
baseline_audit.informal: For PSD matrices and a continuous nonnegative operator-monotone function with $f(0)=0$, $\|f(A)-f(B)\|_2\le f(\|A-B\|_2)$. This converts matrix approximation into approximation of a matrix function without requiring commutation or ordering of $A,B$.
hypotheses: $A,B\succeq0$ are finite Hermitian matrices of the same size
$f:[0,\infty)\to[0,\infty)$ is continuous and operator monotone in every matrix dimension, and $f(0)=0$

sources.label: Theorem X.1.1

baseline_audit.notes: Audited order proof: put t=||A-B||_2, so A<=B+tI and B<=A+tI. Operator monotonicity and scalar concavity imply f(B+tI)<=f(B)+f(t)I by simultaneous functional calculus; reverse A,B. The Hermitian norm/order equivalence finishes. For f(0)>0 apply the result to f-f(0); do not silently identify f(B) with a rank-truncated function of B. Mathlib's operator-monotone predicate and CFC should be reused.

records.readback: The actual operator-monotonicity predicate quantifies over every finite size, with a transport to arbitrary finite index types. Continuity, nonnegativity and f(0)=0 are assumed only on the nonnegative half-line. Scalar concavity and subadditivity are derived using matrix monotonicity, then applied to actual CFC matrices. The sharp spectral-norm modulus covers complex and real PSD inputs, zero differences, singular matrices and empty shapes.

baseline_audit.title: Matrix sign and spectral half-plane projectors
baseline_audit.informal: For a complex matrix with no eigenvalue on the imaginary axis, the sign $S$ is the unique commuting involution for which $SA$ is positive stable. The projectors $(I\pm S)/2$ select the right and left spectral half-planes, including generalized eigenspaces.
hypotheses: $A\in\mathbb C^{n\times n}$, $n\ge1$, and $\operatorname{Re}\lambda\ne0$ for every $\lambda\in\operatorname{spec}(A)$

Positive stable means all eigenvalues have strictly positive real part; $S=\operatorname{sign}(A)$ is defined by primary decomposition, equivalently Hermite interpolation of the locally constant scalar sign
baseline_audit.conclusion: $S^2=I$, $AS=SA$, $\operatorname{spec}(SA)\subset\{z:\operatorname{Re}z>0\}$ characterize $S$ uniquely. $P_\pm=(I\pm S)/2$ satisfy $P_\pm^2=P_\pm$, $P_+P_-=0$, $P_++P_-=I$, with ranges the corresponding generalized spectral subspaces.

sources.label: Chapter 5, equation (5.1), Theorem 5.1 and sign decomposition (5.5); uniqueness derived from commuting invariant subspaces

baseline_audit.notes: The primary-decomposition definition works for defective, nonnormal matrices. The projectors are generally oblique, and the sign need not have norm one. Consumers include invariant-subspace extraction and the Sylvester block identity.

records.readback: Coprime characteristic factors and Bezout evaluation construct the sign for arbitrary matrices with no imaginary-axis eigenvalue. Uniqueness follows from spectral Sylvester separation. The two half-sign projectors are complementary idempotents, and their ranges are exactly the sums of maximal generalized eigenspaces in the two open half-planes.
